lines.line: Cover3
As soon as I got home, I connected to the Net.
A couple of minutes and here I am, staring into the monitor like a black hole, where time stops according to all laws, and reality twists into a bagel.
Foxnet is my secret world, my personal matrix. Here, I can be anyone: a troll queen, a new philosopher in a mask, a shy anime schoolgirl...
Or just be myself, soaking up every bit of text like a sponge, from thread to thread, down to the last crumb.

Pixels danced in my eyes, forming lines, and each line whispered of something secret and hidden. Foxnet was both picture and projector, my personal demon-helper. It guides me on how to live, what to think, how to see.
By five in the morning, it all merged into a single noise, an endless chaos of letters and numbers. And this bleak chaos weighed on me more and more.
Stronger with every hour. But on the other hand - with every hour, it became harder to break away.
My inner voice tried to break through the noise and say something, but the dumb desire to be absorbed by the screen prevailed. And in that moment, I recognized myself.
I am part of this chaos, part of this endless matrix, part of this noise. I belong to forums and chats, these endless web pages, and wikies
And yet, I haven't lost myself. Because my own voice still sounds in my head, even though it is drowned out by the noise.

Sonya and I chatted all night about nothing. I browsed through a whole mountain of hidden forums and pages that would make anyone's hair stand on end. By dawn, my eyes were already barely open from exhaustion.
By morning, they brought me the 'Psyche' I ordered from the page—a sphere for deep dives into the Net. I'd spent all the money I'd stolen from my mom on it.
I've been meaning to ask... Why weren't you at school yesterday?
I decided to stay online. It was pretty lonely, but now it's not. Come by more often.
Your sister goes to school.
Sometimes I find it hard to understand her.
By the way, you have 'Psyche.' We can connect right now.
A chill ran through me. The thought of having to dive into the Net… After such a hard, sleepless night...
My head hurts terribly, but if I want to meet with Kir, I need to bear it.
Alright. Apparently, I have to sacrifice something to maintain communication with Kir.
-Hey, Mira... Are you planning to stay online all day?
-Why?
The cat didn't look as cocky as usual.
-You'll kill yourself. There are plenty of guys around, but you're the only one your mom has.
-I'll manage. Yeah, maybe it's all strange. But I can't help it. There's nothing else to do.
I crawled to the bed, put down the sphere, and pressed my head into it.

Silence. The hiss of capacitors. A flash.
Welcome to Foxnet.
Psyche's service room. In my case, it's just a city square.
A few minutes later, there was a crackling sound.

The world in front of me broke into pixels, as if matter had torn into shreds, and from the shreds formed a whole hurricane of particles that crashed into my body, penetrating and covering me everywhere.

I squinted, and when I opened my eyes, I was in Kir's hugs.

It feels like a dream. Warmth spread across my skin, and waves of cold followed, causing goosebumps and a slight shiver.

I blushed, even though I barely felt the touches. I know this feeling when you hug someone in a dream.

It's like having a warm robe thrown over me that barely touches the skin, or the wind caressing the barely perceptible hairs on my body.

The closer you get to your brain realizing the depth of the feeling, the more you see the falsity around - the floor and walls of cardboard, people a formless, distorted mass, and all words just random sounds, more like bird chirping.
No, it wasn't Kir hugging me, but the same cloud of dead particles.
-Mira? Are you here?
Dissociation… I almost lost connection.
-Yes. Everything's okay. It's all new to me.
-Every time here is new, that's true. And there are so many things to do, you get lost.
I nodded.
-I need a guide to explore Psyche… I'm scared to do it alone.
-Alright.
Kir smiled kindly. I like his smile. Condescending and sincerely kind.
I held out my hand to him, and he took it. For some reason, I got nervous, and my hands began to disintegrate into pixels.
-Come on. Pull yourself together.
His voice gave me a bit of confidence, and the falling particles returned to their place and trembled impatiently.
-It's so strange… It looks like we're molded from sand.
-What's surprising, if even our real bodies were sculpted by God from clay?
-What... Really, from clay?
Kir spread his arms.
-It only takes a slight loss of faith in the reality of what's happening, and this reality collapses, like the Tower of Babel.
-And everything you've built and experienced is worthless, it's all just sand and dust.
-But if I take off the sphere and think that everything is unreal, the world will not cease to exist.
-Who knows... Maybe you just need to believe in it more strongly.
-Haven't you dreamed of something as a child, something impossible that later came true?
-Let me think...
-I didn't find a phone under my pillow, but I really wanted it.
-But on the other hand… When I begged God for my mom to come when she was gone for a long time… She always came.
I sighed heavily.
-Do you miss her?
-No. I regret it. I should have asked for a phone.
Kir burst into hysterical laughter.
-Alright. Then... Blink seven times, clap three times, do a backflip, and by morning...
-Kir!
-Okay, okay… Here!
A brand new phone appeared in my hands.
-Hey... How did you...
-You just have to want it badly enough, and you can give any shape to a handful of sand.
-But it's still not real.
-You offend me. It's the realest.
-Sure, of course.
-You can check for yourself.
The phone's screen really lit up as soon as I pressed the button. Everything was in place - the symbols and numbers from 0 to 9.
All that was left was to dial a number. It's nonsense, of course, but... I'll call Sonya.
I remember her number by heart.
Ringing... Nothing. No answer.
I'll try again.
The hissing on the line turned into static, a knock, and finally...
-Hello? Hey?
-Sonya, is that you?
-Yes, it's me. Why are you calling? Missed me?
-I... No, nothing. Forget it.
-Uh... Alright.
-So... Is my brain tricking me, right? None of this is real, and Sonya didn't answer?
-Our brain deceives us all our lives, and we see the world as it 'came up' with it.
-In reality, there are no colors, smells, sounds. There is only endless energy, making space clump and move.
-All we can do is simplify it into understandable things, so we don't go mad.
-Here, in the simulation - you are a cluster of energy. A cluster of charged particles running along wires. A radio wave. Here, look.
Kir jumped up and hovered in the air.
-Come on, you try it too.
-Okay...
I squatted and jumped, trying to grab onto the air as if it were something solid, but my hands just wouldn't grip, and I fell back down.
-I don't think I can...
-Just needs a bit of practice.
Kir picked me up, and I squealed in surprise.
I pressed myself to his chest and wrapped myself in his warm jacket.
He smelled nice, like grapes and wheat…
We easily rose to a great height, and I felt my insides tighten and drop somewhere to my feet. I closed my eyes - the clouds around us parted in smoky tufts.
-Just don't look down...
-It's a shame. It's beautiful down there.
-Alright... Then, put me down somewhere, and I'll look around.
We ended up on the Tower's roof. I'd never been here before - the staircase to the top was locked.
Gathering my courage, I looked down at the city, as if plunging my face into ice water. The ground - patched together like a quilt. A pattern of glowing windows and lanterns...

My eyes were dazzled, causing a headache. Everything felt so calm and restless at the same time, and it made me a little nauseous... If not for the cool wind cooling my forehead and cheeks, I would have thrown up by now.
Kir walked up and stood beside me, leaning on a concrete block.
-Listen...
-Yes?
-Why do you always talk to me so strangely?
I put on a serious face and stared at the confused Kir. My question caught him off guard.
-What do you mean?
-Well... People don't talk the way you do. All these metaphors. Why?
-I don't know, honestly. Maybe it's the old-school upbringing. Something like aristocratic heritage.
-Then why me? I'm not like you. I think I'm not interesting to you.
-You're wrong; it's not like that at all...
-And this computer. You're the one who left it for me, not Sonya.
-I knew you'd figure it out. I just wanted you to accept the gift without suspicion.
-Why all this?
-Just… I am really into you.
-Wh… What?
I urgently need to get out of here. But we're on the roof!
As much as I hate to admit it, there's only one way out.
This is a virtual world; nothing can happen to me, right?
Fuck it!
I jumped off the ledge into the black abyss.
-Mira!
Kir immediately ran toward the concrete blocks, but I didn't see what happened next.
It feels like falling in a dream, but this one is long and drawn-out. I wonder why I haven't woken up yet...
The Tower's windows blur into a single glowing column.
Boom.

Out of fear, I closed my eyes. Metal clinked sharply across the concrete floor, followed by stones and earth falling around me.
Afraid to look around, I groped around with my hands - finding bits of debris and dust.
-Achoo!
Where am I?
It's dark all around. Only  monitors flicker somewhere in a long, long concrete tunnel. The awful, rotten smell made me cover my nose.
-Did something die here?
The echo rolling through must mean only one thing - this labyrinth stretches for hundreds of meters in both directions.
It seems like no one has been here in a long time - the place looks abandoned. That smell...
The smell of death, no - the smell of a forgotten past, if it had a smell. The void sighed sadly and frighteningly, and a breeze tickled my legs.
So, there's another exit somewhere? I looked up, where there was a hole in the ceiling, sand and bits of plaster trickling down.
From here, the Tower seemed to reach the very dome of the sky, while I was at the very bottom. I need to hurry before Kir catches up to me.
Anyway, no matter where you go, it's damp and gross everywhere.
My shoes' soles slapped against the floor, echoing off the walls. I wonder where I'm going... It keeps getting darker and darker.
If only I had a flashlight... Kir can create things somehow; why can't I?

Wow, it's just like in those stupid magic tales.
Okay.
In the flashlight's beam, it's much easier to move. Even despite all those scary shadows that look like monsters when the beam runs over debris.
This is definitely some old bunker from the Big War. In this world, it's located right under the tower...
I wonder if such a bunker exists in reality? I'd ask Sonya… But she'd probably chicken out.
Amid hundreds of meters of concrete, the beam outlined the distinct edges of a heavy metal door.
Some kind of room, or another corridor?
There were marks on the door, as if someone had broken the lock rather than opened it with a key. So, surface people were here before me.
Odd that it's so clean here, not even any graffiti with tags.
The entire floor in the room is flooded with murky water. Wild bundles of wires converge at a mountain of monitors.
Some nonsense is on the screens—static and colored stripes. Is this the bunker observer's office?
Doesn't seem like it... There are old metal shelves with flickering lamps everywhere. Looks more like computing equipment, but very old.

Wow, really, electronics running on tubes...
Tiny and big tubes... And then... Very large ones...
From the large tube, through foggy yellowed glass, a pair of eyes stared back at me. I jumped back.
-What the fucking hell is going on here?!
-Oh, there you are.
I shuddered and turned around.
-Kir, what is this place? This madness couldn't possibly be in my memories!
-Well, who knows what you might have imagined… What scared you?
-Oh… I see. It's a human brain and eyes.
-Why are you so calm about this? It's not normal!
-As far as I can understand, it's a neuroaccelerator. Like how Psyche uses your brain to build worlds, this setup uses a brain to speed up calculations...
-Whose brain is it?
-Who knows... Back then, human lives weren't considered very important.
The veins in the brain swelled and contracted again, which meant that the brain was still alive, and it might even see everything happening here right now.
Something hit my throat, and I ran out of the room, pushing Kir aside.
-Why did you come here anyway? It's damp and dirty. If I were you, I'd never come here.
-I'm always sticking my nose where it doesn't belong...
-Well, no big deal. Let's go back up.
Kir lifted me back to the surface.
-Actually, this was supposed to be something romantic...
-I know. Sorry for ruining it.
-The main thing is, if you do this next time, don't mix up reality with the network.
-Will there be a next time?
-Why are you saying that... We've only known each other for a couple of days... And... It's not like we've talked much...
-I'm not very good at understanding human emotions. Sorry.
-Oh, come on! Why are you acting so weird again... You're scaring me!
-What are you afraid of? Could I hurt you?
-Sometimes it feels like… You can do anything.
Kir laughed awkwardly.
-Only what can be done with the Net.
-So, really anything...
-Ha-ha...
An awkward silence fell. Kir was gathering his thoughts, staring at his feet and scuffing floor with his shoe, while my mind felt completely empty.
-Shall we go for a walk together?
I nodded. We descended down to the square near the tower. The loose tiles squished underfoot as if we were walking on the ruins of an ancient civilization.
It's nice that the cars around us hum along the road, blending into a single continuous noise. After all, we're in the very center of the city.
-Kir, tell me, why are there even cars here?
-Why do you think they're driving, even though it's just the two of us here? There aren't actually people behind the wheel.
-Then who?
-Shells. Beings that act on a simple algorithm... Or ghosts.
-Ghosts?
-They disappear the moment you try to talk to or touch them.
Random people you see on the street appear as ghosts, or become empty shells.
-And what about my friends?
-Your friends stay the way they are. Or rather, the way they wanted you to see them.
-So they're not real people... And I wasn't talking to the real Sonya on the phone...
-What do you mean by 'real'? To you, Sonya won't change. She'll stay as you remember her.
And the more people connect to the network, the more her personality will resemble the 'original' Sonya.

Kir held out his hand, and I took it.
I think I blushed...
It's been so long since I last walked here. In this place, you feel like part of a big, strong city.
A concrete giant, sleeping an eternal slumber. You feel its breath like the pulse of the earth beneath your feet, like the roar of cars racing through its arteries.
It never speaks, and it seems emotionless, but you feel that calming, cool touch of concrete against your back if everything in your life has gone wrong.
It doesn't wish you harm, although it can kill you if necessary. The city is a huge, powerful beast that loves you, its flawed, awkward child.
-But how… Sonya has her own personality! She has her own self… A simulation can't have its own personality!
-You think so? Do you have a personality?
-Well... Of course I do!
-And the choices you make... You make them consciously? You control every step, and there's nothing above your mind and your 'self'?
I shook my head.
-I don't know… I don't know anything. It can't be that something controls everyone. This world is so dumb and insane...
-What kind of jerk would have to be running everything for it to be this messed up?
-I don't know either... Maybe only here, in an artificial world, a person can start to mean something and act the way they want?
-If only it were possible to turn your brain into ones and zeros...
I stopped and took both his hands, looking into his empty, icy eyes.
-Aren't you afraid of losing yourself? Why aren't you scared to dive headfirst into the network?
What if this mush of ones and zeros, what you so badly want to become, what if it erases you?
-To lose yourself, you first have to find yourself. And I never found myself. That's why it's easier for me...
-I think you're exaggerating.
I smiled warmly.
-Don't be so hard on yourself.
-Thanks for agreeing to meet. Anyway... We've talked for so long...
-Yeah... It's time for me to wake up, too.
Kir dissolved into a million pieces, and I disconnected.
With trembling hands, I took off the sphere.
Oh... I'm so exhausted.
No, no, if I dive into the network again, my brain will just melt...
I crawled over to the toilet, pushed myself up on my hands, and leaned against the rim with trembling hands.
A lump stuck in my throat, refusing to go forward or back, tormenting me and keeping me from breathing. That's it, I can't. I lay down on the cold rim, closing my eyes.
I have never... Never felt this bad before...
After a while, the nausea passed, leaving a headache behind. Pulling myself away from my porcelain friend, I got up on my knees and somehow managed to stand upright.
That was a mistake. The image in front of my eyes filled with darkness, and...
A dark, musty corridor filled with wires and rusty pipes. I'm almost sure there's a layer of ground above me.
For some reason, this place seems very familiar… Where could I have seen it before? The sounds of relays and electric impulses whisper something all around me, but I don't understand a thing.
-Is there anyone here?
My voice shattered against the wall and echoed down the corridors.
And again, nothing. I'm alone here.
Bright flashes, indistinct words, and bits of memories flickered in my head, and none of it fit together.
A faint light appeared from the depths of the corridor. It trembled, flickered, like a spark in a night forest. I crawled towards it, like a moth to a porch lamp.
The light led to a door. I wonder what's behind it... I pressed my ear against the cold metal, trying to make out words.
-Wake up... And help me... wake up...
-Oh god, how can you sleep when someone's yelling 'Wake up!' in your ear?
-I... I think I passed out.
-Did you even sleep today?
-No, did you?
-Neither did I!
-How are you always so energetic...
-Deal with it; I was born this way.
-I saw... It was either a dream... or...
-What was it?
-I think it's connected to the being that's calling me...
-I ended up in a long, long corridor, where everything was tangled in wires, and I heard a voice there… I finally understood it.
-Sonya, I have to find this place. This being is waiting for me. I have to go to it.
-Maybe you're... you know... losing it?
-I... I believe that you really feel all of this, but... I'm just worried about you.
-No, no... I'm definitely in my right mind! I'm just asking… Help me! Help me find it.
-I don't think I can do it alone. I don't even know what to do...
-Let's look in the school library books. Maybe you saw this place in a textbook, and it showed up in a dream.
-Do you think I've ever opened a textbook?
-Ha! What am I even saying… Let's go.
I was filled with a strange sense of excitement and didn't notice the way to school until we were standing in front of the library building.
It's the largest book storage in the whole city - not only students come here, but also those who have nothing better to do than pick up a book. Gosh, what nerds!
Anyway, we're about to step into enemy 'nerd' territory.
I slammed a dusty book shut, raising a small cloud. Sonya sneezed.
-It's so cozy here! If it weren't for the 'Silence' rule, I'd skip school here all the time.
-Oh please… They wouldn't even let us play Pokemon cards here.
-So, in conclusion...
Sonya sat on a chair, facing its back, gripping it between her knees.
-We know that your monster is somehow connected to the occult and the church...
-So this creepy thing from your dreams is something mystical or like that?
-I'm not sure, but it says here about the Beast. It calls to people when they sleep and takes them into its world if they respond.
-So that means we need to continue our search… in a church? Do we even have a church?
Sonya glanced around the reading room and gasped in surprise.
-Mira, look, look!
In the reading room, right across from us, sat a priest.
Yep, it's the priest from the Christian club...
He looked up at the shouting Sonya, and we awkwardly approached the bench where a bearded old man in a black cassock sat. He smelled  bad.
It's clear he spends days holed up in his church basement - his clothes smell like candles, dampness, and sweat. Maybe it's the smell of holiness.
-I know about the Beast.
He immediately put his book aside and stared at me with wide-open eyes.
-The Beast? How do you know about the Beast?
-Oh, I knew I'd be exposed someday. Lord forgive me, a sinner.
Sonya and I exchanged glances but said nothing. The huge figure of the priest rose from the bench and headed for the exit, and we followed him like a train.
After leaving the school gate, we turned into an alley and then onto a parking lot. Looks like we're going to the garages.
Sonya and I exchanged glances again; her eyes held a mix of fear and her constant thirst for adventure.
Oh, Sonya, how I understand you. I also don't really want to end up enslaved by this smelly guy.
Colorful garages appeared out of the orange haze, on our left and right, and finally, we stopped in front of one of the containers.
The priest inserted a key into the lock, looked around fearfully, and silently unlocked the door.
-Uh… God, what is that?!
Out of the darkness came a small silver figure with unnaturally narrow eyes and stared at me coldly and detachedly.
From that gaze, I felt as if my soul was retreating somewhere back, and a black hole had opened in my chest, trying to swallow me whole.
An eerie, endless emptiness. With difficulty, I looked away.
-What? I thought you came because... Never mind.
With a rude shove, the priest sent the alien back into the container, locked the door, cursed, and disappeared.
-Okay, this is definitely not what we need.
-Agreed.
I slammed the dusty book shut, raising a small cloud. Sonya sneezed.
-It's so cozy here! If it weren't for the 'Silence' rule, I'd skip school here all the time.
-Oh please… They wouldn't even let us play Pokemon cards here.
-So, in conclusion...
Sonya sat on a chair, facing its back, gripping it between her knees.
-We can say with confidence that your monster lives in an old, old military bunker.
-Sounds very boring... and unclear. Where are we supposed to look for it?
Sonya seemed to remember something and thought.
-Weird things are happening at my house. First, there was this strange smell, out of nowhere. Some kind of rotten, earthy smell...
-I'm used to the garbage smell in my apartment, but this one was different... Suffocating, with a metallic aftertaste.
-At first, it only smelled in the bathroom, then it spread to the kitchen, the bedroom, everywhere. It's like it filled every corner...
-Everything stinks in this city. No surprise there.
-Yeah, but... Then a crack appeared on the wall, and at night there was a faint knock, as if someone was tapping from inside the wall.
-Maybe the bunker is right under my house.
-We could go check it out right now. Even though I think it's all because you're just messy.
-I haven't been to your place in ages...
We opened the door, and I immediately smelled the odor Sonya was talking about.
-Whoa, what a stink.
It felt like I was in a dark, damp basement. In the time I hadn't been to Sonya's, her apartment had turned into some kind of pigsty.
-When did you last clean up here?
Sonya shook her head.
I tried flipping the light switch, but the light didn't come on - there was no bulb in the socket.
-Here, look!
I came closer to Sonya, examining her little den in detail.
-Careful!
My sneakers almost slipped into a wide crack in the floor, which looked like a half-open eye.
-And is this where you hear the noise?
Sonya nodded.
-Darn, we need something long to see how deep it is.
-I don't think I have anything... Maybe just...
Sonya knelt down and stuck her hand into the crack. Slowly her hand went lower and lower, first her wrist, then her elbow was inside, but there was no bottom.
Already her wrist and elbow were inside, but there was still no bottom. I got braver and knelt beside Sonya, lowering my arm almost to my shoulder.
Something soft and cold brushed against my fingers. Sonya and I both screamed at the same time.
-That was me touching you, you idiot!
Sonya calmed down a bit and sat down on the floor.
-So, there's some kind of basement under my apartment... Maybe even a bunker!
-Not exactly something to be happy about... Is this the hole that stinks? Let's plug it with something...
We found a few old things in the closet and stuffed them into the crack. Now it just needed to be aired out, and she'd be able to live peacefully again.
-It's a shame we can't fit in there ourselves...
-If it's a basement or bunker, there must be a regular entrance somewhere.
-You're probably right.
So, did I skip school today?
Maybe I'll still make it to the last lesson.
The usual road, maybe even too usual. I think I could walk to school with my eyes closed because I've done it a thousand times.
Just imagine! So many times... And each time feels like the first. Butterflies in my stomach from the sight of glowing, fluffy balls of light, drifting in the night.
Usually, only the sounds of my own footsteps, dripping water, and the gentle wind fill the background - that's why I stopped. Something's wrong...
As if coming out of a trance, I turned toward the trash cans.
At that moment, the strange sounds stopped. I froze, like a cat on the hunt, waiting.
It seemed like footsteps were coming from somewhere behind the trash can. Should I go check?
-Hey, I see you!
I wonder why some bum sleeping in a dumpster would care to know...
The sound of feet slipping, a short cry, and right in front of me lies Alina.
My eyes, as wide as saucers, stared at the miserable-looking girl.
Groaning, she got up and awkwardly looked away.
-Alina, you... What were you doing there? Were you following me?
She turned her head, like a child caught doing something bad.
There was a dirty smear of food in the corners of her mouth - I doubt she was here because of me.
-Are you... Are you eating from the trash?
Tears welled up in her eyes, and Alina was about to cry.
-Why?
-I... I have no money...
-Is Tolik not giving you money for food?
She shook her head.
Moistening a sleeve with spit, I wiped the dirt off her face.
-I guess I'm not going to make it to school on time...
-Yeah. Classes are already over...
-Even better! Come on, I know what to do.
-Was there really no other way than scrounging around trash bins like a damn pigeon?
-Don't insult... Pigeons...
-Why?
-They were raised by humans to carry letters… And then they were abandoned.
-Abandoned when they were no longer needed. And now the birds are dying on the streets...
-They don't even know how to build nests...
Her words carried a grievance against humanity. She puffed up, like a real pigeon, and pouted.
-But you can't take them all home...
-I would take them... But my dad won't let me.
-What if you took just one?
-Still no. Maybe… Maybe you could take one?
-Me?
-Yeah… You live alone...
-Here, see? This is Mo-mo.
Alina pointed to a white pigeon missing a toe on its left foot.
Mo-mo seemed to understand what her 'owner' wanted, and flew over, landing on her shoulder.
-So... When you have time… We'll come get her, alright?
-I'll try to find a place for her on my balcony. I hope she'll be okay...
-I can't. I live with a cat.
-A... a cat?
-Well, something like that.
-I get it... I wasn't really hoping anyway...
Alina pulled a piece of bread from her pocket and coaxed a flock of pigeons, who had been watching us from the wires.
They immediately recognized her and, with a flurry, rushed for the crumbs, surrounding Alina in a solid ring.
-So... Where are we going?
-We're going to school.
-W-why? I just came from there...
-I want you to stop eating from dumpsters...
Alina thought for a moment, and finally blurted out:
-You want to get me a job?!
-Yeah.
-But no one will take me... At my age, I won't be able to get a job anywhere...
-It's better to talk to the principal.
-I'm scared of him... Do you think you can do it?
-I'm not afraid. You can trust me.
-Alright...
Alina slumped and curled up, dreading the thought of the principal. After all, he often calls her in to talk about her absences.
-A-are you just going to walk into his office and ask him for me?
-Nope. I want us to have a trump card... I want to find a skeleton in his closet.
-W-what do you mean, skeletons in his office?
-Well, not literally... I mean, I want to sneak into his office.
-You're always like this… Isn't there a legal way...
I shrugged.
-I'm afraid not. Not in our town.
The school was almost empty. No one was in the yard, and of the students, only those left to study after hours remained.

I always loved that feeling when you walk down the quiet halls, where the lights are still on, all alone.

Footsteps echoed off the sickly blue walls, and it's hard to believe that just recently these halls were crowded with students.

In complete silence, we slipped into the principal's office; he wasn't there.
-Probably off drinking tea with someone again. Do principals do anything besides drinking tea?
The door swung open abruptly, and Alina shrank against the table. I barely had time to put everything back as it was.
-What... are you doing here?
-W-we... We accidentally, we...
Alina jerked, trying to run from the office, but I grabbed her hand.
-Wait.
-I came for a reason.
-Mira, what business could you have in my office? Who even let you in?
-The door was open... I want to talk... about Alina.
He awkwardly hesitated in the doorway and went to his desk, throwing himself down in his chair with importance.
-Alright... Let's talk.
-You see... Alina has a difficult situation, and... she needs a job...
-Even if it's something simple. Maybe just cleaning... Or helping in the workshop... or library...
-Mira, you know I can't let her work without her parents' consent...
-You can go... Alina, take a seat, let's talk. Maybe some tea?
Alina jumped up and shouted imploringly:
-No, no, no, just not there, I'm not sitting there!
The principal paled and froze, pointing to the chair across from him.
-No, Alina will get a job right now, or everyone will find out about you!
-W-what will they find out? Mira, what are you saying?
His voice sounded less confident than usual. It seemed to work!
-I know that you spy on the kids. And I know about the cameras. I'll tell everyone at school!
The principal looked like a trapped mouse; it was almost pitiful to watch.
-Alina's dad is a cop!
-I understand! I understand! No need to shout...
-If you harm Alina...
-I won't! Let's go.
He barely lifted himself from his chair, which seemed to be sucking him back in, and led us out.
-So... where would you like to work?
-I'd like to... take care of the library.
The librarian was surprised, but didn't object.
Alina was assigned the duties of putting misplaced books back, dusting, watering plants, and covering for the library lady when she wasn't around.
Just basic chores.
Alina immediately 'started her duties' - they handed her a broom from the supply room. The adults left us in the library alone.
-Mira, I... I can't express how grateful I am to you... No one has ever... done anything like this for me before...

She was glowing with happiness... I'm glad I helped her. That smile, the sparkle in her eyes... I don't know why, but I would give a lot to see her happy.
Such a strange feeling...
-And... If you want, you can come to me anytime - we can cook together... So you don't go hungry.
-Mira, you're the best friend! I've always dreamed... of cooking with someone... It's so cool that we'll be together...
-We could go to my place right now.
Alina shook her head.
-I think I'd better get used to things here first... Probably strange to skip work on the first day.
-I'll sort out that pile of new books and put them on the shelves...
-Alright.
I turned to leave.
-Mira...
-Yeah?
-Do you think... it's okay that... we won't tell anyone what the principal is doing?
-It definitely won't help us... And between protecting a few strangers, and protecting you - I'll always choose the latter.
-And... I suggest you do the same if you want to survive.
-I understand... It's very harsh, but... I guess I'll listen to you.
We finally said goodbye.

What a day... I'd light up a cigarette if I knew how.
I sat down on the steps by the entrance, staring blankly into the night sky.
It couldn't say a word to me, but I felt guilty. Some strange pain was churning inside me.
Am I a good person or a bad one? Have I acted all this time like someone who does good?
What do my choices lead to... Maybe if I hadn't chosen anything at all, things would be so much better?
Honestly, staring at the sky, it makes me want to give up. What's the point, when you're just a grain of sand?

No matter what you do, the stars will remain in their places, unaware of your existence.
And then I noticed one of the stars starting to twinkle and even seemed to be getting larger.
-Huh? What is that?
I rubbed my eyes.

Yep... The light kept getting bigger.
After a few minutes, it was very close. Didn't look like a star...
Oh no, it's a burning airplane... How'd it get here?

Something started falling from the plane.
Instead of hiding, I for some reason walked out into the open and looked up into the sky.
It was a rain of paper. Hundreds of sheets fluttered after the plane, separating from the swarm, landing on rooftops, falling onto the road, sinking into puddles.
Catching one mid-air, I was able to examine it in detail. It had words printed on it, strangely overlapping with all the other madness.
Everything around me became one big, colorful carousel.
What could all of this mean?
The plane disappeared with a roar into the clouds.
-What nonsense.
I tossed the leaflet into a puddle and trudged home.
I stopped and froze at the entrance.
-What's that noise? Please, don't let it be Mom coming home...
I found the cat trying to clean the frying pan, holding a metal scrubber in his paws.
-Well, I'll be damned.
-Hello to you too, buddy.
-And... what are you doing here?
-Cooking dinner. What's it look like, epta?
-Wow, turns out you can do something other than annoy me.
-You could help, you know.
Why not. Cooking with a cat. An imaginary cat. Doesn't sound too bad.
-Let's make pike head soup!
-Ew!!! Just thinking about it makes me sick...
We agreed to make a regular fish soup. Simple dish, but I'm no chef.
Purr-Purr began tearing apart the fish with his claws. I was in charge of the vegetables. Good thing there were still a couple of carrots left in the kitchen cabinet.
